Published online:
    September 2, 2026

Geographic focus:
    Canada, North America

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES] — covers BoC rate decision and Q2 GDP rebound
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — December hike pricing, oil price trajectory, tariff effects
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — forecast for multiple hikes through 2027, sustained inflation risks from energy

Synopsis:
    The Bank of Canada held its policy rate at 2.25% but shifted to a markedly hawkish tone. Governor Macklem signaled readiness to hike multiple times if inflation — currently at 3%, driven by oil near $90/bbl vs. the BoC's $75 assumption — stays elevated. Canada's strong Q2 growth (3.3% annualized) provides room to tighten. U.S. tariffs add uncertainty but are seen as a limited direct drag. Markets now price a 25bp hike by December and ~3 additional hikes in 2027. The BoC dropped its "rates are at the right level" language, a significant hawkish signal.
